title: Microsoft says October updates didn’t actually fix VPN issues
description: Microsoft acknowledged that the October 2026 Windows 11 cumulative updates did not fix a known bug affecting Always On VPN connections. The issue causes VPN connections to remain stuck in a connecting state or fail, sometimes showing an error about ports already in use. Microsoft mistakenly marked the bug as resolved in October but reverted it to mitigated status, promising a fix in a future update. A temporary workaround involves configuring Always On VPN to use a single tunneling protocol (SSTP or IKEv2) instead of automatic protocol selection.
aiSummary: A bug affecting Always On VPN connections on Windows 11 24H2 and later was initially reported after the September 2026 updates, causing connection failures when automatic protocol selection or fallback was enabled. Microsoft released October 2026 cumulative updates that were mistakenly flagged as resolving the issue. The company later clarified that the problem remains and that a fix will be included in an upcoming update. Meanwhile, IT administrators are advised to mitigate the issue by configuring VPN profiles to use either SSTP or IKEv2 exclusively rather than automatic protocol selection.
aiImpact: The bug disrupts Always On VPN connectivity, causing connections to hang or fail, which can impact users' ability to securely connect to corporate networks. This affects devices running Windows 11 24H2 and later with Always On VPN configured for automatic protocol selection. The issue may cause operational disruptions for organizations relying on Always On VPN for secure remote access.
